To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multiplicity distributions can be affected by a multiplicity-dependent efficiency and that a multiplicity-dependent detector efficiency can be modeled using a simple formula.
a multiplicity-dependent efficiency changes the characteristic of a baseline distribution, and that this effect is quantified by the moments and their derivative properties.

(i) a multiplicity-independent efficiency does not change multiplicity distributions, while a multiplicative multiplicity-dependent efficiency does; (ii) the multiplicity-dependent efficiency affects the mean, variance and higher moments, but does not change the shape of the distribution; (iii) multiplicity-dependent efficiency changes the derivative quantities such as skewness, kurtosis, and their ratios, but not the ratios of moments.
